title: 阿里巴巴通过在香港发售股票为人工智能业务筹集100亿美元
content:
Alibaba Group raised HK$80 billion ($10.2 billion) in Hong Kong's largest follow-on share offering, with the company saying it will use all net proceeds to invest in its AI infrastructure. That transaction, which closed Sunday, marks Hong Kong's largest share sale since Prosus NV, the technology-investment firm, divested $14.7 billion worth of Tencent Holdings stock in 2021, according to Bloomberg.
The company sold 710 million shares at HK$112.70 each; the price represented a 3.6% discount to where Alibaba's U.S.-listed shares closed on Friday. The offering drew institutional demand amounting to roughly three times the available shares, Bloomberg reported, citing people with knowledge of the transaction.
Alibaba stock fell 8.5% on Monday, its steepest single-day drop since early 2025. Despite the decline, Chairman Joseph Tsai purchased about HK$80 million worth of Alibaba stock, and Chief Executive Officer Eddie Wu acquired about HK$40 million, according to the outlet, citing filings with the Hong Kong stock exchange.
The offering is being made exclusively to non-U.S. persons in offshore transactions, the company said. The company said it plans to direct all net proceeds toward its full-stack AI strategy, with a particular focus on building out and improving the underlying infrastructure that supports it. China International Capital Corp., HSBC Holdings, Morgan Stanley, and UBS Group arranged the deal. Under the terms of the deal, Alibaba cannot sell additional shares for 90 days.
The capital raise is part of a broader push by Alibaba to compete in AI development. Alibaba has pledged to put more than 380 billion yuan ($56.5 billion) toward AI over three years, with the investment covering chips, data centers, and large-language model development. Alibaba's Qwen model family is the world's most popular by downloads.
Alibaba has been selling non-core assets to fund that expansion, including a deal to divest its gaming unit, Lingxi Games, to Trustar Capital for at least $1.5 billion. Earlier divestitures included stakes in hypermarket chain Sun Art and department-store operator Intime for a combined $2.6 billion in late 2024. Its cloud division posted revenue of 41.63 billion yuan in its most recent quarter, up 38% year-over-year, with AI-related revenue extending a streak of triple-digit year-over-year growth to 11 consecutive quarters.
Baidu, Alibaba's domestic rival, has no plans for a comparable equity offering, a company spokesperson said, saying its current cash reserves and operating cash flow are adequate.

report.summary: 阿里港股募资102亿美元，全部投入AI基础设施。
report.background: 阿里巴巴完成港股80亿港元（约102亿美元）后续股票发行，成为香港市场2021年以来最大规模增发。公司明确将全部净募集资金用于AI基础设施投入，并承诺三年内投入超3800亿元人民币支持AI战略，覆盖芯片、数据中心和大模型研发。为集中资源，阿里已出售游戏、商超等非核心资产。此次募资正值国内AI竞争加剧，而百度表示暂无类似股权融资计划。
key_points: 阿里通过港股配售融资约102亿美元，为香港2021年以来最大后续发行，发行价较美股收盘折让3.6%。
全部资金将投向全栈AI战略，重点改善底层基础设施，且交易后90天内不得再增发股票。
机构认购需求约3倍超额，但消息公布后阿里股价单日下跌8.5%，董事长和CEO分别增持约8000万和4000万港元。
阿里三年规划投入超3800亿元人民币于AI，覆盖芯片、数据中心和大模型，Qwen系列为全球下载量最高开源模型家族。
为维持资本开支，阿里持续出售非核心资产；云业务最新季度收入同比增38%，AI相关收入连续11个季度三位数增长。
report.impact: 对AI行业而言，阿里大规模募资将强化其在中国云和AI基础设施领域的竞争地位，拉动算力产业链投入。对开发者，Qwen等开源模型及云平台有望获得更持续的资源支持，使用门槛可能降低。对普通用户，AI应用和云服务迭代会更快，但亿级资本开支也可能带来短期成本转嫁或市场集中度提升。
report.tools: 可关注阿里云百炼平台、ModelScope魔搭社区、Qwen系列开源模型（如Qwen2.5及最新版本），以及阿里财报中AI资本开支与云业务增速数据。
